name: Hyperosmia Enhancement
description: Expands the olfactory epithelium and increases olfactory receptor gene expression by a factor of 50, approaching canine-level smell sensitivity. Unlike the Jacobson's Organ modification which adds a new chemical sense, Hyperosmia enhances the existing sense of smell to extraordinary levels. The user can track scent trails hours old, identify individuals by body chemistry, detect trace chemicals at parts-per-billion concentrations, and smell emotional states through stress hormones and adrenaline. The world becomes a landscape of smell — every room has a history written in scent, every person carries an olfactory autobiography. Helix Biosystems' version includes a conscious attenuation system that allows the user to 'turn down' the sensitivity when it becomes overwhelming. Street versions lack this feature, leaving users at the mercy of every garbage bin, perfume cloud, and unwashed body in the city.
source_organism: Canis lupus familiaris (domestic dog, bloodhound variant), Ursus arctos (brown bear, olfactory receptor genes)
procedure: Nasal epithelium retroviral treatment, single session
reversibility: Reversible with olfactory receptor suppression; may leave permanently enhanced baseline
side_effects: Sensory overload in crowded or unsanitary environments
Nausea from detecting smells others can't perceive
Food becomes overwhelmingly complex — some foods become inedible due to detectable off-notes
Street versions have no attenuation — users in the Gray Zone's densest neighborhoods suffer constant olfactory assault
Strong perfumes and cleaning chemicals become physically painful
social_perception: Practical and sympathized with. Bloodhound users are valued as trackers, investigators, and quality control inspectors. The social cost is visible — enhanced-smell users often cover their noses in public and avoid crowded spaces. In the Gray Zone, unattenuated users are pitied.
story_hooks: A Bloodhound user detects a chemical signature in a building that they recognize from a classified Helix Biosystems facility — a compound that shouldn't exist outside the lab
A Scent Hound investigator tracks a missing person through three districts by smell alone, only to discover the trail was deliberately laid as a lure
